tests.mutation: MultipleAircraft.AtTheSameTime prohibited the person who is in a role for one aircraft (`aircraft.Length <= 0` for `aircraft.Length <= 1`, the finding's Permitted), so none and one unmanned aircraft came back prohibited; this test went red, 4 of its 5 findings failing Assert.True. It went red too with MultipleAircraftFinding.Authority citing waivable-regulations' `§ 107.205` instead of single-aircraft's `§ 107.35`.

MultipleAircraft.AtTheSameTime permitted two unmanned aircraft (`aircraft.Length <= 2` for `aircraft.Length <= 1`), so a person in one of the three roles for N1 and N2 at the same time came back permitted; this test went red.

MultipleAircraft.DistinctAircraft stopped counting the aircraft a person only observes (`engagement.Role != AircraftRole.VisualObserver && seen.Add(engagement.Aircraft)` for `seen.Add(engagement.Aircraft)`), so a remote pilot in command of N1 acting as visual observer for N2 counted one aircraft and came back permitted; this test went red.

MultipleAircraft.AtTheSameTime skipped its own gate check (`is { } suspended && suspended.Reason == UnresolvedReason.UnsupportedRule` for `is { } suspended`), so a stated waiver of § 107.35 resolved to a finding instead of declining OutsideCurrentScope -- and with dependsOn empty there is no other entry's gate to decline in its place; this test went red.

Waivers.Suspension treated every statement as a waiver in force (`return true` for `return statement.InForce`), so a statement that none is held still declined OutsideCurrentScope instead of resolving; this test went red.

Waivers.Suspension compared the statement's regulation with itself (`statement.Regulation, statement.Regulation` for `statement.Regulation, regulation`), so a waiver of § 107.51 was accepted as one of § 107.35; this test went red, no exception being thrown.

Handlers.SingleAircraft defaulted a missing statement to none held (`request.Waiver ?? WaiverStatement.NoneHeld(MultipleAircraft.Regulation, "the engine")` for `Demand(request.Waiver, ...)`); this test went red.

Handlers.SingleAircraft defaulted missing engagements to none (`request.Engagements ?? []` for `Demand(request.Engagements, ...)`), so a request that said nothing about the aircraft resolved as though the person were in no role for any; this test went red.
Handlers.SingleAircraft defaulted a missing person (`request.Person ?? "a person"` for `Demand(request.Person, ...)`); this test went red.

`Handlers.SingleAircraft` demanded the typed input ahead of the rule's § 107.205 gate -- the ordering thirteen of the fifteen gated entries took before #93 -- by wrapping the argument back up (`Demand(request.Person, request.EntryId, nameof(request.Person))` for `request.Person`). A caller stating a certificate of waiver of § 107.35 in force and describing nothing else was then refused `ArgumentException` naming `Person` -- `FactRequired`, `MissingInput=Person`, filed under `Outstanding`, which `OperationEvaluation.Outstanding` documents as "everything the caller still owes this engine" -- instead of being declined `OutsideCurrentScope` citing § 107.205 (`docs/decisions/0008-the-waiver-gate-precedes-every-other-demand.md`). So this test, which pins one answer for a waived request, the same across every gated entry, went red on both target frameworks: `Failed!  - Failed:     3, Passed:   740, Skipped:     0, Total:   743` for net10.0 and the same figures for net8.0. The others red with it were `WaiverGateOrderingTests.Nothing_a_stated_waiver_suspends_is_reported_as_something_the_caller_still_owes`; `WaiverGateOrderingTests.A_waived_request_is_never_asked_for_a_typed_input_the_waiver_has_made_irrelevant`.
